notes: cpi/CN: the April 2012 CPI edition stores a fixed-base index (y/y = 12-month ratio inside the vintage); the published y/y behind the one-full-month publication gate competes, and the published y/y (latest 2012-03) is used as the fresher series.
policy/IN: BIS monthly differs from the daily month-end in 2007-03; monthly rows retained.

policy/TR: the one-week repo rate became the policy rate on 2010-05-20 (the BIS series switches from the overnight borrowing rate, 6.50% → 7.00%). The switch is not a rate change (CBRT Monetary Policy Committee decision No. 2010-16, 18 May 2010: overnight rates kept unchanged; as a 'technical rate adjustment', 'the one week repo rate, which becomes the new policy rate, is set at 7 percent—50 basis points above the overnight borrowing rates'): earlier history is spliced by +0.50pp so that policy changes are measured on the new instrument.

cli.label: April 2012
cli.basis: dated public report quoting this edition's figures

evidence.label: 24/7 Wall St, 'OECD Indicators Point to Economic Growth', 10 Apr 2012 (10:04 ET): the index of composite leading indicators for OECD members rose to 100.5 in February from 100.3 in January; the euro area reading of 99.6 was flat
The Skeptical Speculator, 'Stocks plunge in Europe as Spanish and Italian yields surge', 11 Apr 2012: the OECD's overall composite leading indicator rose to 100.5 in February from 100.3 in January

method_note.text: This edition is the first in which the OECD CLI targets GDP instead of the index of industrial production as its reference series ('From April 2012 therefore the OECD has switched to using GDP as the reference, ceasing to rely on the IIP as an intermediate target'); the whole history in the vintage was re-estimated, so its levels are not comparable with earlier editions. The model scales growth by each series' own dispersion within the vintage.
method_note.label: OECD, 'OECD System of Composite Leading Indicators', April 2012 (methodology guideline by G. Gyomai and E. Guidetti; PDF created 10 Apr 2012, the release day)
